title: Introduction to GradBoostR
text: GradBoostR provides regression binary-classification models implemented Rcpp RcppArmadillo. package includes random forest regression, gradient boosting regression, neural network regression, decision stumps, fast binary random forest classification. main regression interface consists : gradboostr_fit(), fits model; gradboostr_predict(), generates predictions fitted model. method argument selects regression engine: Specialized lower-level functions include fit_stump(), rf_class_fit_fast(), rf_class_predict_fast(), rf_class_predict_prob_fast(). vignette demonstrates complete workflow: generate reproducible regression data; fit baseline regression models; examine prediction errors residual diagnostics; tune model hyperparameters using cross-validation; compare --fold regression errors; fit decision stump; evaluate binary classifiers using held-observations; visualize hard-class regions class probabilities. Training-set diagnostics presented explain model behavior. Cross-validated held-results used discussing predictive performance.
code: method = "rf" method = "gbm" method = "nn"

title: Introduction to GradBoostR
text: regression examples use synthetic data set three predictors. response depends primarily X1, smaller negative contribution X2, includes normally distributed noise. X3 contribute directly response therefore acts uninformative predictor.
code: set.seed(864)  n_reg <- 120L X_reg <- cbind(   X1 = rnorm(n_reg),   X2 = rnorm(n_reg),   X3 = rnorm(n_reg) )  y_reg <- (   2.0 * X_reg[, "X1"] -   0.5 * X_reg[, "X2"] +   rnorm(n_reg, sd = 0.7) )  regression_data <- data.frame(   X1 = X_reg[, "X1"],   X2 = X_reg[, "X2"],   X3 = X_reg[, "X3"],   Response = y_reg )  head(regression_data, 8) #>           X1          X2          X3    Response #> 1  0.8259430 -1.21770927  0.79702852  2.72873606 #> 2  1.6837055 -0.40938819  0.96225350  4.21391230 #> 3 -2.9104891  0.09768491  0.17461701 -5.31318501 #> 4  1.8750856  0.14468638  0.02812713  3.53754995 #> 5  0.6510606  1.66285955 -1.69835956  0.01615669 #> 6 -0.7975370  0.01234072  0.45650717 -1.21428786 #> 7  1.1283158  0.69479572 -0.73021125  2.07743833 #> 8  0.7023991 -1.05993568 -0.29250443  0.59055968 ggplot(regression_data, aes(X1, Response)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.7, colour = "steelblue") +   geom_smooth(     method = "lm",     formula = y ~ x,     se = FALSE,     colour = "firebrick",     linewidth = 0.8   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   labs(     title = "Synthetic Regression Data",     subtitle = "The response contains a strong contribution from X1",     x = "X1",     y = "Response"   )

title: Introduction to GradBoostR
text: Two local helper functions support regression examples. rmse() calculates root mean squared error. scale_train_validation() standardizes training matrix applies center scale validation matrix. Calculating preprocessing statistics training fold prevents information validation fold leaking model fitting.
code: rmse <- function(actual, predicted) {   sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2)) }  scale_train_validation <- function(training_data, validation_data) {   training_center <- colMeans(training_data)   training_scale <- apply(training_data, 2, sd)   training_scale[!is.finite(training_scale) | training_scale == 0] <- 1    scaled_training <- sweep(training_data, 2, training_center, FUN = "-")   scaled_training <- sweep(scaled_training, 2, training_scale, FUN = "/")   scaled_validation <- sweep(validation_data, 2, training_center, FUN = "-")   scaled_validation <- sweep(scaled_validation, 2, training_scale, FUN = "/")    list(train = scaled_training, validation = scaled_validation) }

title: Introduction to GradBoostR
text: Gradient boosting builds additive ensemble sequentially. learning_rate controls contribution fitted tree, n_trees controls number boosting iterations.
code: gbm_model <- gradboostr_fit(   X_reg,   y_reg,   method = "gbm",   learning_rate = 0.1,   n_trees = 50 )

title: Introduction to GradBoostR
text: Neural networks can sensitive differences predictor scale. predictors therefore standardized fitting. fitted model uses one hidden layer. hidden controls number hidden units, epochs controls number training iterations, learning_rate controls update size.
code: X_reg_scaled <- scale(X_reg) set.seed(273)  nn_model <- gradboostr_fit(   X_reg_scaled,   y_reg,   method = "nn",   hidden = 10,   epochs = 50,   learning_rate = 0.01 )  nn_prediction <- gradboostr_predict(   nn_model,   X_reg_scaled,   type = "response" )  stopifnot(   inherits(nn_model, "gradboostr_model"),   identical(nn_model$method, "nn"),   is.numeric(nn_prediction),   is.null(dim(nn_prediction)),   length(nn_prediction) == nrow(X_reg_scaled),   all(is.finite(nn_prediction)) )  nn_rmse <- rmse(y_reg, nn_prediction) nn_rmse #> [1] 2.107537

title: Introduction to GradBoostR
text: gradient boosting prediction API return one finite numeric prediction observation. Prediction error defined observed response minus predicted response. Positive errors indicate underprediction, negative errors indicate overprediction. Gradient boosting training-error diagnostics  Points close dashed diagonal line represent predictions close observed responses.  Residuals distributed around zero without clear pattern indicate limited systematic error. Curvature smoothed line can indicate structure remains unexplained.   Q-Q plot descriptive. Departures reference line can reveal skewness, heavy tails, isolated large errors.
code: gbm_prediction <- as.vector(   gradboostr_predict(     gbm_model,     X_reg,     type = "response"   ) )  stopifnot(   inherits(gbm_model, "gradboostr_model"),   identical(gbm_model$method, "gbm"),   is.numeric(gbm_prediction),   is.null(dim(gbm_prediction)),   length(gbm_prediction) == nrow(X_reg),   all(is.finite(gbm_prediction)) )  gbm_prediction_error <- y_reg - gbm_prediction gbm_absolute_error <- abs(gbm_prediction_error) gbm_squared_error <- gbm_prediction_error^2  gbm_rmse <- sqrt(mean(gbm_squared_error)) gbm_mae <- mean(gbm_absolute_error) gbm_mean_error <- mean(gbm_prediction_error) gbm_median_error <- median(gbm_prediction_error)  gbm_error_summary <- data.frame(   Metric = c(     "Mean error",     "Median error",     "Mean absolute error",     "Root mean squared error",     "Error standard deviation",     "Minimum error",     "Maximum error"   ),   Value = c(     gbm_mean_error,     gbm_median_error,     gbm_mae,     gbm_rmse,     sd(gbm_prediction_error),     min(gbm_prediction_error),     max(gbm_prediction_error)   ) )  knitr::kable(   gbm_error_summary,   digits = 4,   caption = "Gradient boosting training-error diagnostics" ) gbm_diagnostic_data <- data.frame(   Observed = y_reg,   Predicted = gbm_prediction,   Error = gbm_prediction_error )  ggplot(gbm_diagnostic_data, aes(Observed, Predicted)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.7, colour = "darkorange") +   geom_abline(     intercept = 0,     slope = 1,     colour = "firebrick",     linetype = "dashed",     linewidth = 0.8   ) +   coord_equal() +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   labs(     title = "Gradient Boosting Observed versus Predicted Values",     subtitle = paste(       "Training RMSE =", round(gbm_rmse, 4),       "| MAE =", round(gbm_mae, 4)     ),     x = "Observed",     y = "Predicted"   ) ggplot(gbm_diagnostic_data, aes(Predicted, Error)) +   geom_hline(     yintercept = 0,     colour = "firebrick",     linetype = "dashed",     linewidth = 0.8   ) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.7, colour = "darkorange") +   geom_smooth(     method = "loess",     formula = y ~ x,     se = FALSE,     colour = "black",     linewidth = 0.8   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   labs(     title = "Gradient Boosting Residual Diagnostic",     subtitle = "The black curve highlights systematic error patterns",     x = "Predicted",     y = "Prediction error (observed - predicted)"   ) ggplot(gbm_diagnostic_data, aes(Error)) +   geom_histogram(     bins = 20,     fill = "darkorange",     colour = "white",     alpha = 0.85   ) +   geom_vline(     xintercept = 0,     colour = "black",     linetype = "dashed",     linewidth = 0.9   ) +   geom_vline(     xintercept = gbm_mean_error,     colour = "firebrick",     linewidth = 0.9   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   labs(     title = "Gradient Boosting Prediction-Error Distribution",     subtitle = paste(       "Mean error =", round(gbm_mean_error, 4),       "| Median error =", round(gbm_median_error, 4)     ),     x = "Prediction error (observed - predicted)",     y = "Count"   ) ggplot(gbm_diagnostic_data, aes(sample = Error)) +   stat_qq(alpha = 0.7, colour = "darkorange", size = 1.8) +   stat_qq_line(     colour = "firebrick",     linetype = "dashed",     linewidth = 0.8   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   labs(     title = "Gradient Boosting Residual Q-Q Plot",     subtitle = paste("Residual SD =", round(sd(gbm_prediction_error), 4)),     x = "Theoretical normal quantiles",     y = "Observed residual quantiles"   )

title: Introduction to GradBoostR
text: candidate learning rate, 50-tree gradient boosting model evaluated using three folds. Mean validation RMSE summarizes predictive error, standard deviation shows variability across folds. Gradient boosting learning-rate results
code: gbm_learning_rate_values <- c(0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)  gbm_learning_rate_results <- do.call(   rbind,   lapply(seq_along(gbm_learning_rate_values), function(rate_index) {     current_rate <- gbm_learning_rate_values[rate_index]     fold_rmse <- numeric(n_folds)      for (fold in seq_len(n_folds)) {       training_rows <- fold_id != fold       validation_rows <- fold_id == fold       set.seed(4000 + rate_index * 100 + fold)        model <- gradboostr_fit(         X_reg[training_rows, , drop = FALSE],         y_reg[training_rows],         method = "gbm",         learning_rate = current_rate,         n_trees = 50       )        prediction <- as.vector(         gradboostr_predict(           model,           X_reg[validation_rows, , drop = FALSE],           type = "response"         )       )        fold_rmse[fold] <- rmse(y_reg[validation_rows], prediction)     }      data.frame(       Model = "Gradient boosting",       LearningRate = current_rate,       MeanRMSE = mean(fold_rmse),       SDRMSE = sd(fold_rmse)     )   }) )  gbm_learning_rate_results <- gbm_learning_rate_results[   order(gbm_learning_rate_results$MeanRMSE), ] row.names(gbm_learning_rate_results) <- NULL  knitr::kable(   gbm_learning_rate_results,   digits = 4,   caption = "Gradient boosting learning-rate results" ) ggplot(gbm_learning_rate_results, aes(LearningRate, MeanRMSE)) +   geom_errorbar(     aes(       ymin = pmax(MeanRMSE - SDRMSE, 0),       ymax = MeanRMSE + SDRMSE     ),     width = 0.003,     colour = "grey40"   ) +   geom_line(colour = "darkorange", linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_point(colour = "darkorange", size = 3) +   scale_x_log10(breaks = sort(gbm_learning_rate_values)) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   labs(     title = "Gradient Boosting Learning-Rate Analysis",     x = "Learning rate (log scale)",     y = "Cross-validated RMSE"   )

title: Introduction to GradBoostR
text: neural-network comparison uses 10 hidden units 50 epochs every candidate learning rate. Scaling recalculated inside training fold prevent preprocessing leakage. Neural-network learning-rate results
code: nn_learning_rate_values <- c(0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10)  nn_learning_rate_results <- do.call(   rbind,   lapply(seq_along(nn_learning_rate_values), function(rate_index) {     current_rate <- nn_learning_rate_values[rate_index]     fold_rmse <- numeric(n_folds)      for (fold in seq_len(n_folds)) {       training_rows <- fold_id != fold       validation_rows <- fold_id == fold        scaled_fold <- scale_train_validation(         X_reg[training_rows, , drop = FALSE],         X_reg[validation_rows, , drop = FALSE]       )        set.seed(5000 + rate_index * 100 + fold)        model <- gradboostr_fit(         scaled_fold$train,         y_reg[training_rows],         method = "nn",         hidden = 10,         epochs = 50,         learning_rate = current_rate       )        prediction <- as.vector(         gradboostr_predict(           model,           scaled_fold$validation,           type = "response"         )       )        fold_rmse[fold] <- rmse(y_reg[validation_rows], prediction)     }      data.frame(       Model = "Neural network",       LearningRate = current_rate,       MeanRMSE = mean(fold_rmse),       SDRMSE = sd(fold_rmse)     )   }) )  nn_learning_rate_results <- nn_learning_rate_results[   order(nn_learning_rate_results$MeanRMSE), ] row.names(nn_learning_rate_results) <- NULL  knitr::kable(   nn_learning_rate_results,   digits = 4,   caption = "Neural-network learning-rate results" ) ggplot(nn_learning_rate_results, aes(LearningRate, MeanRMSE)) +   geom_errorbar(     aes(       ymin = pmax(MeanRMSE - SDRMSE, 0),       ymax = MeanRMSE + SDRMSE     ),     width = 0.002,     colour = "grey40"   ) +   geom_line(colour = "dodgerblue3", linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_point(colour = "dodgerblue3", size = 3) +   scale_x_log10(breaks = sort(nn_learning_rate_values)) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   labs(     title = "Neural Network Learning-Rate Analysis",     x = "Learning rate (log scale)",     y = "Cross-validated RMSE"   )

code: set.seed(623) n_stump <- 200L X_stump <- cbind(   X1 = rnorm(n_stump),   X2 = rnorm(n_stump),   X3 = rnorm(n_stump) ) y_stump <- ifelse(   X_stump[, "X1"] > 0,   3 + X_stump[, "X2"],   -3 + X_stump[, "X2"] ) + rnorm(n_stump, sd = 0.4)  stump_model <- fit_stump(X_stump, y_stump)  predict_stump <- function(X, model) {   feature <- model$feature + 1L   ifelse(     X[, feature] <= model$threshold,     model$left_val,     model$right_val   ) }  stump_prediction <- predict_stump(X_stump, stump_model) stump_rmse <- rmse(y_stump, stump_prediction)  stump_summary <- data.frame(   FeatureIndex = stump_model$feature + 1L,   Threshold = stump_model$threshold,   LeftValue = stump_model$left_val,   RightValue = stump_model$right_val,   TrainingRMSE = stump_rmse )  knitr::kable(   stump_summary,   digits = 4,   caption = "Fitted decision-stump parameters" )

title: Introduction to GradBoostR
text: classification_metrics() calculates threshold-dependent metrics hard class predictions. roc_curve_data() evaluates sensitivity false-positive rate across probability thresholds. auc_from_roc() calculates trapezoidal area ROC curve. confusion_plot_data() prepares observed predicted classes visualization.
code: classification_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {   actual <- as.integer(actual)   predicted <- as.integer(predicted)    tp <- sum(actual == 1 & predicted == 1)   tn <- sum(actual == 0 & predicted == 0)   fp <- sum(actual == 0 & predicted == 1)   fn <- sum(actual == 1 & predicted == 0)    precision <- tp / max(1, tp + fp)   recall <- tp / max(1, tp + fn)    data.frame(     Accuracy = (tp + tn) / length(actual),     Precision = precision,     Recall = recall,     Specificity = tn / max(1, tn + fp),     F1 = if (precision + recall == 0) {       0     } else {       2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)     }   ) }  roc_curve_data <- function(actual, probability) {   thresholds <- sort(unique(c(Inf, probability, -Inf)), decreasing = TRUE)    points <- lapply(thresholds, function(threshold) {     predicted <- as.integer(probability >= threshold)     tp <- sum(actual == 1 & predicted == 1)     tn <- sum(actual == 0 & predicted == 0)     fp <- sum(actual == 0 & predicted == 1)     fn <- sum(actual == 1 & predicted == 0)      data.frame(       Threshold = threshold,       TPR = tp / max(1, tp + fn),       FPR = fp / max(1, fp + tn)     )   })    result <- do.call(rbind, points)   result[order(result$FPR, result$TPR), ] }  auc_from_roc <- function(roc_data) {   roc_data <- roc_data[order(roc_data$FPR, roc_data$TPR), ]   sum(     diff(roc_data$FPR) *       (head(roc_data$TPR, -1) + tail(roc_data$TPR, -1)) / 2   ) }  confusion_plot_data <- function(actual, predicted) {   as.data.frame(     table(       Observed = factor(actual, levels = c(0, 1)),       Predicted = factor(predicted, levels = c(0, 1))     )   ) }
